topStories.headline: SFMTA Unanimously Approves New Parking and Transit Lane for Chinatown
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency voted to add all-day parking and a new 24-hour transit-only lane on Clay Street, aiming to balance merchant needs with faster Muni service.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Chinatown will gain more all-day parking and a full-time transit lane after the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency unanimously approved a proposal at its July 21 board meeting. The project, presented by SFMTA Project Manager Jessica Kuo, focuses on changes to Clay and Sacramento streets near Portsmouth Square — a stretch heavily used by the neighborhood's small businesses and transit riders alike.

The approved plan converts part-time tow-away spots to all-day parking on two blocks of Clay Street between Kearny and Leidesdorff streets, as well as on one block of Sacramento Street between Powell and Stockton streets. At the same time, the middle lane on Clay Street between Kearny and Leidesdorff will become a dedicated 24-hour transit-only lane, primarily serving Muni's 1-California line.

The project reflects a longstanding tension in Chinatown. According to SFMTA data, about 72 percent of Chinatown households do not own a car, making transit reliability critical for residents. At the same time, small businesses depend on curb access for customers and deliveries. The 1-California line, which connects the Richmond District through Chinatown to downtown, serves more than 20,000 riders each day and has historically had slow travel times in the area.

Project Manager Kuo expressed confidence that improved curb management — including cameras on buses to discourage illegal parking in the transit lane — would help enforce the new configuration. Construction is expected to begin before the end of summer 2026.

topStories.headline: Lower Nob Hill Housing Tower Rises Past Eighth Floor
topStories.dek: The 22-story, 303-unit mixed-income tower at 1111 Sutter Street has cleared a major construction milestone, with concrete now past the eighth floor as of late June 2026.
topStories.body:
Construction is moving steadily at 1111 Sutter Street in San Francisco's Lower Nob Hill neighborhood, where the concrete frame of a 22-story residential tower cleared the eighth floor as of late June 2026. The project — developed by Martin Building Company and built by general contractor Nibbi Brothers — represents one of the most significant mixed-income housing developments currently underway in San Francisco.

The 303-unit complex is designed to include 101 below-market-rate (BMR) apartments, or roughly a third of all units, designated for lower-income residents. The unit mix spans studios, one-, two-, three-, and four-bedroom apartments. Planned amenities include a two-level fitness center and an on-site public childcare center. The project uses union labor across all trades and is backed by financing from the AFL-CIO Housing Investment Trust and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

The project has been years in the making. Mayor Daniel Lurie joined a groundbreaking ceremony at the site in December 2025, and the Board of Supervisors earlier approved special financing measures to keep the development on track amid high construction costs and interest rates. The developer has said the project should reach completion within approximately 23 months of breaking ground.

The tower, designed by David Baker Architects, sits on what was previously a vacant lot and a small commercial structure at the intersection of Sutter Street — adding dense, publicly subsidized housing to a neighborhood already well-served by transit and services.

topStories.headline: Mark Hopkins Hotel Celebrates Centennial with Revived 100-Martini Passport at Top of the Mark
topStories.dek: The InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco is marking 100 years atop Nob Hill with a year of celebrations, including the return of its legendary 100-Martini program at its iconic 19th-floor sky lounge.
topStories.body:
The InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco is celebrating a major milestone in 2026: the hotel's 100th anniversary, with its official centennial date falling on December 4, 2026. As part of a year-long series of curated events, historical tributes, and special programming, the hotel's celebrated sky lounge, Top of the Mark, revived its famed 100-Martini experience on Memorial Day Weekend, May 25, 2026.

Guests at the 19th-floor lounge can now work through a passport-style menu of 100 martinis — ranging from classic preparations to contemporary spirit-forward cocktails priced between $22 and $26 — and collect stamps as they go. Completing the full list earns a special prize. The promotion is set to run at least through December 4, 2026.

The hotel, which opened atop Nob Hill in 1926, has been a defining feature of San Francisco's skyline and hospitality landscape for a century. It sits at the intersection of three cable car lines and has hosted diplomatic functions, society gatherings, and countless personal milestones over its history. Internationally acclaimed bandleader Alex Mendham and his 11-piece orchestra have also launched a monthly series of elegant dance evenings in the hotel's Peacock Court ballroom as part of the centennial programming.

For Nob Hill residents and San Franciscans eager to mark the occasion, Top of the Mark remains open nightly, offering panoramic views of the city and bay alongside its centennial cocktail menu.

moreNews.headline: ArtHaus Partners Acquires 117-Unit Nob Hill Apartment Tower for $25 Million
moreNews.body: Oakland-based ArtHaus Partners, in partnership with Belay Investment Group, closed on the acquisition of The Terraces — a 13-story, 117-unit rent-controlled apartment building at 1300–1330 Bush Street in Lower Nob Hill — for $25 million in late May 2026. The purchase price of approximately $212,000 per unit represents a significant discount to the building's 2011 foreclosure price of $30.4 million. The company, formerly known as Riaz Capital, plans to rebrand the property as ArtHaus Terraces and has said it focuses on preserving naturally occurring affordable housing. Housing advocates have noted the repositioning of rent-controlled units warrants close monitoring.

moreNews.headline: FITNESS SF Announces Fall 2026 Opening for New Polk Gulch Gym
moreNews.body: San Francisco-based gym chain FITNESS SF is set to open its newest location at 1600 Jackson Street — the former Lombardi Sports building — in September 2026, bringing a 42,000-square-foot facility to the Polk Gulch neighborhood. The gym will serve Russian Hill, Nob Hill, and surrounding areas and will feature strength and cardio floors, group fitness classes, personal training, recovery amenities, a dog room, and over 70 parking spaces. Founding memberships are currently available at pre-sale pricing ahead of the public opening.

moreNews.headline: The Huntington Hotel Reopens on Nob Hill After Years-Long Closure
moreNews.body: The Huntington Hotel at 1075 California Street on Nob Hill is welcoming guests again following a multi-year closure. Named one of 2026's most anticipated hotel reopenings by ELLE Décor and Vogue, the reimagined property offers 71 guest rooms and 72 suites with bay and city views, a legendary three-story spa, and the return of The Big Four restaurant in its 50th anniversary year. The hotel, originally constructed in 1922 and added to the National Register of Historic Places in September 2025, has been restored with fresh global influences while preserving its original Georgian architectural elegance.

moreNews.headline: Nob Hill Residential Infill Project Proposed at 1728 Larkin Street
moreNews.body: A new residential infill proposal has surfaced for 1728 Larkin Street in Nob Hill, where developer Equity Six LLC is seeking to build a six-story structure with nine apartments — including one one-bedroom, six two-bedrooms, and two three-bedrooms — under San Francisco's recently passed Family Zoning Plan. The roughly 85-foot-tall building, designed by RG Architecture, would yield approximately 16,420 square feet of total floor area, with about 10,925 square feet dedicated to housing. The project would reduce on-site parking from five to two spaces.

restaurants.description: Michelin-starred contemporary Chinese restaurant on Waverly Place, helmed by chef Brandon Jew, blending Cantonese technique with California ingredients in a historic Chinatown banquet hall.

restaurants.name: Empress by Boon
restaurants.description: Sixth-floor fine dining destination with panoramic Chinatown and North Beach views, featuring Michelin-starred Chef Ho Chee Boon's elegant seasonal modern Cantonese tasting menu.

restaurants.name: China Live
restaurants.description: Expansive multi-concept space on Broadway featuring a tea lounge, marketplace, restaurant, and the exclusive Eight Tables by George Chen, pairing classic Chinese dishes with local California ingredients.

restaurants.name: Good Mong Kok Bakery
restaurants.description: Legendary Chinatown dim sum counter known for its generously stuffed char siu bao and pillowy pineapple buns, drawing daily lines outside its compact Stockton Street storefront.

restaurants.name: R&G Lounge
restaurants.description: Multi-level Chinatown institution celebrated for its iconic salt-and-pepper crab, live seafood tanks, and classic Cantonese banquet-style dishes.

restaurants.name: House of Nanking
restaurants.description: Beloved, no-frills Chinatown fixture famous for its chef-driven menu of Shanghainese dishes fused with local ingredients — and the tradition of the chef choosing your meal for you.

restaurants.name: Sam Wo Restaurant
restaurants.description: One of Chinatown's oldest legacy restaurants, serving traditional Cantonese dishes including congee, noodles, and roast meats in a historic multi-story setting on Clay Street.

restaurants.name: Far East Café
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest banquet-style Chinese restaurant, operating since 1920, known for its private curtained booths and traditional Cantonese family-style dishes.

restaurants.name: Fiorella Polk
restaurants.description: Casual, well-loved Polk Street outpost of the Richmond original serving light-crusted Neapolitan-style pizzas topped with clams, pepperoni, or guanciale, plus antipasti in a spacious, welcoming room.

restaurants.name: Del Popolo
restaurants.description: Born as a cult-favorite mobile wood-fired pizza truck, now a beloved Lower Nob Hill restaurant serving puffy, perfectly charred Neapolitan pies alongside great wines in a cozy dining room.

restaurants.name: Amelie
restaurants.description: Romantic Polk Street French wine bar with an extensive list of natural and small-producer wines, intimate candlelit atmosphere, and a small menu of French-inflected bites.

restaurants.name: Bob's Donuts
restaurants.description: Beloved round-the-clock Polk Street donut institution, a Nob Hill neighborhood institution since 1960, famous for its fresh-made donuts and the iconic giant donut challenge.

restaurants.name: Kinjo
restaurants.description: Intimate omakase sushi counter on Polk Street helmed by a master chef, earning a Michelin star for its seasonal, creative nigiri and sashimi preparations in a quiet neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Dunya Bistro
restaurants.description: Warm Polk Street bistro offering generous portions of Mediterranean staples — hummus, kebabs, mezze, and grilled meats — in a casual and welcoming neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Z & Y Peking Duck
restaurants.description: Chinatown restaurant celebrated for its expertly prepared Peking duck — perfectly crispy-skinned and served tableside — alongside a broad menu of traditional Chinese dishes.

restaurants.name: VIP Coffee and Cake Shop
restaurants.description: Neighborhood cha chaan teng modeled after a traditional Hong Kong tea restaurant, offering pastries, noodle soups, Hong Kong milk tea, and egg tarts in a casual, homey setting.

restaurants.name: Goldenette
restaurants.description: Popular Polk Street Vietnamese restaurant serving bowls, banh mi, and elevated comfort dishes in a bright, modern space drawing a loyal neighborhood crowd.

restaurants.name: Street Restaurant and Bar
restaurants.description: Lively Polk Street neighborhood gathering spot with a broad menu of American comfort food, rotating craft cocktails, and a buzzy happy hour popular with Polk Gulch locals.

restaurants.name: Outta Sight Pizza
restaurants.description: Chinatown's only pizza slice counter, serving excellent thin-crust pies with classic toppings as well as creative grandma-style specials including Peking duck and hoisin.

hotels.name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco

hotels.name: Nob Hill Inn

shops.description: San Francisco's legendary working fortune cookie factory on Ross Alley, where visitors can watch cookies made by hand on cast iron griddle wheels and purchase custom and flavored varieties.

shops.type: Artisan cheese and specialty food shop
shops.description: Well-curated Polk Street specialty shop offering an extensive selection of domestic and imported cheeses, charcuterie, pantry items, wine, and gourmet provisions.

shops.name: Cole Hardware
shops.description: San Francisco-owned neighborhood hardware institution with a Polk Street location serving Nob Hill and Russian Hill residents with tools, home goods, and expert staff.

shops.name: Polk Street Market
shops.description: Neighborhood convenience market on Polk Street housing a celebrated deli counter renowned for its rotisserie chicken sandwiches and the stacked San Franpsycho sandwich.

shops.name: Chinatown Kite Shop
shops.description: Long-running Chinatown specialty shop selling hand-crafted kites, Chinese folk toys, lanterns, and colorful novelties along Grant Avenue.

shops.name: Lark Books

artEntertainment.name: Great Star Theater
artEntertainment.type: Historic Chinese theater and performance venue
artEntertainment.description: The oldest Chinese theater in the United States, founded in 1925 as the Great China Theater, now presenting Cantonese opera, film screenings, cabaret, and Asian cultural performances in the heart of Chinatown.

artEntertainment.name: Grace Cathedral
artEntertainment.type: Episcopal cathedral and cultural event space

artEntertainment.description: Legendary 19th-floor cocktail lounge inside the InterContinental Mark Hopkins, offering 360-degree panoramic views of San Francisco and the bay, currently featuring the centennial 100-Martini passport program.

artEntertainment.name: 41 Ross Gallery (CCC SF)

gymsRecreation.description: A uniquely San Franciscan yoga experience held beneath the soaring Gothic nave and luminous stained glass of Grace Cathedral, with live music accompaniment and instruction open to all levels.
